title: A Figure Twice Read

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: A slate is read for the moot and again for those who come late, and the figure is the same both times. The pot does not care which reading you counted, and the hand that cannot reach the handle is written in neither.
epigraph.attribution: A saying of the pot board in Low Kiln, in the kiln month

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a one-hundred-and-ninety-eight-to-two-hundred-day-old body carried everywhere and told by nobody — six months and eighteen days to six months and twenty days, no roof with a word for it. The surgeon's register colours the noticing (a cost asked as a direction answered with the pot and the weather, a carried arm as a record in muscle that knows weight and not cost, the private file turned out as instruments on a towel, likenesses taken down one at a time before they can stand up and call themselves a rule, a figure read twice that is still not the figure paid, and an inch of a small hand asked again under a roof the market cannot enter) without a present-tense Chicago break or a tagged remembered line — the old life stays offstage — and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, collector or back-room interior, no new hearing, no tenth stopping, no third gap, no fourth likeness made a cause, no seventh green, no seventh sighting, no calling of the loan, no payer named, no private record read and no ending

scenes.title: The Hand before the Reading
scenes.synopsis: First entry, first dated heading and drop capital: Day 198, Ember 19, Ninthday, small hours under the Vail kiln-house roof, then before first grey and into the morning at the hearth, the loaf shelf's low angle and the Clay Yard. Do not recap the close of Chapter 48 and do not re-read the longest holding as a sign. Open on the hand outside the wool going up an inch toward the note of water over water through the finger's-width door and coming down; the count at one hundred and ninety-seven is carried into the new morning, exact, complete and unspent, and the boy is one hundred and ninety-eight days old and six months and eighteen days and nobody says so (T071/T072). First smell hot clay under tallow and wet wool with the sour mineral breath of the unswept corner; first sound the kiln drawing in fours with a gap, not a bell. The crust lies leathery two inches from his ear, its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread of drool frozen and unwiped; cold stopped at cheek, temple and the small bare joint at the wrist where the wool rides back, the afterdrop waiting on a warming nobody in this house will perform. The carried fire gives four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and ninety-eight days (T088); through the finger's-width door the river keeps its note of water over water, a fifth low thing never counted among the hearings; overhead the boards keep four nails, four, and a knot the width of a thumb — three counts in three places that do not become one, because a man who wanted them to agree would have to put a payer under them and none stands to any (T061/T082). Sella gives every instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket, says the house, keeps her half-pace, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze without touching it, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale off the coals, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with her hand resting a half-beat longer at the setting, feeds him gruel from the house's own dish with the spoon on her sleeve and not his mouth, and tells the fire it is the thaw and The house will keep it (T058/T079). The widow's mark hangs where it hung — a morning and a shelf are not openings and there has been no opening since before the kiln on Ember 1. A neighbour at the threshold with dry mud-scurf on her hem asks what the firing will want now the second reading stands a day off; the cost goes to the pot and the weather and arrives nowhere, nothing priced, refused or entered (T077; the figure up the road in Berr's locked box stays offstage, T015/T041/T047 held). The sweet edge of lead glaze comes up off High Kiln on a wrong wind and is answered as a direction, not a second edge paid (T064 held). At the note through the door the hand goes up an inch and is asked to stay; it comes down before the counted breath has finished — a shorter holding, the body keeping its own time — and is filed on a place of its own beside the others, not a hearing, not a seventh, not a stopping, not a payment, not one of the three held changes, not a key, not a power and not a rule, no payer named (T061/T082). He still cannot close the two inches to the pot handle, lift the crust or speak a number. Ember's second Account-day and market stand one day off on Day 199; the market does not get to read the inch. Forward, not closed.

scenes.title: The Figure Kept Out of the File
scenes.synopsis: Second entry of Day 198, no new dated heading: afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf, the hearth, the kindling, the wheel-shed edge, the clay road at the going of the light and the bed. The afternoon thins without ending, heat going first off the high air and staying longest in the low places under the shelf, behind the pot, in the fold of wool; the underside of the loaf shelf makes a roof that stops at the edge of his reach and the heat comes down that roof in a slow slant and stops at the same place, as if it too had been given an instruction. Sella stands with her back to the basket, moves her lips along a row standing with two unnamed gaps (the old space at the row's end and the palm's breadth that came in on the night of Seed 6) and gives nobody a figure; one glance at the clay jar with her hand shutting half over nothing; her finger stays on top of the shelf's front edge and does not go beneath, so the charcoal tally stays unread, uncounted, uncopied, and the Day 166 held beat stays where it was left (T100). She tells the fire it is the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, stands with the back of the pot counting under her breath toward no opening (the small intake, the hold, the letting go), pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, lets her hand rest a half-beat longer at the setting than the setting needs, and does not look toward the bed (T058/T079). At the kindling the small knife lies at the edge of its sill, six counted in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh at the lip where it cannot, Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it; Tarn takes the broom only after it has been instructed, tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, says Yes, house to an early thaw and a late while wanting the late because it puts off the paying, and sweeps the collector's road without turning; no collector comes. His chest is tight since the dark; Ash is worked into his knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line and the pale clip-ring at his left wrist holds what light there is; the ear-sentence comes all the way to the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name, the Seed 16 breath is drawn and not spent, nine stoppings stay nine objects with no tenth before the seventh year is earned, the seventh year stands nearer its end than it has ever stood and has not given, the loan is uncalled, and his stroke goes over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check (T036/T076). In the wheel-shed Jorra gives the men who went into the back room before first grey no name and does not say the room was cold, keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray, tells the wheel it does not care whose hands and a pot You'll do, knows the full note three turns ahead and withholds it from a man on a wrong wind whose saying about a pot singing before its time stays a saying about a pot and is not made true as a lesson, no pot lost (T035/T031/T062, T065/T095). When Sella's voice goes low and unfinished, his bent finger goes into the cold damper and holds until the sentence reaches the pot, then the tongue moves a hair's breadth and the finger is left standing — a remembered repetition, not a change made again, not paired with Day 161, 166 or 171; the iron is one piece with two bites and no word in Grathic carries both mercies (T062). He's not Vail stays sealed and the promise of the boy's name stays ungiven. At the going of the light she carries him home up the clay road with the instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket, woodsmoke before her in long low bars and river wind behind with the taste of water over water, the carrying arm a record in muscle that remembers weight and not cost, going wide around the pan's gone round ring, the bare dark trough whose water is called weather, the space beneath the lowest rack with its broken birth-slates, the field's empty place and the place the carriers crossed, each with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098). Under the roof she sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without a look at his face, leaves the thread frozen, banks the coals with the back of a broken pot, and the fire keeps four low pulls with its fifth missing for a hundred and ninety-eight days. In the small hours he lays out the file as a man lays instruments on a towel: six hearings beside and never among with the sixth out of a person and no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and unpaid, the told bell beside the heard and the told figure beside the paid, three held changes on three places, the loft scrape on a fourth and the carried man's pale line on a fifth, the held inch on a sixth, the crust's gap, the shelf's two gaps, the pan's gone ring and the field's empty place on trays that do not touch, no third gap, no fourth likeness, no finger drawn, the stone cold in its pot in the loft, the charcoal unread, the Seed 16 breath unspent and the loan uncalled (T061/T082, T006, T064, T060/T086/T097, T100). The market's figure, read or to be read, is not entered in any of it; a figure read aloud is not the figure paid, and the read figure lies beside the paid and never becomes one. Forward, not closed.

scenes.title: The Second Reading over the Basket
scenes.synopsis: Third entry, third dated heading, the chapter's hinge: Day 199, Ember 20, Tenthday, the second Account-day and market-day of the kiln month, before noon through the morning at the Cross, the reading block, the moot-post, the pot board, the stalls and the out-of-line landing. The district keeps calling Tallow the firing month and Ember the kiln month and neither is corrected. The boy is one hundred and ninety-nine days old and six months and nineteen days and nobody says so (T071/T072); the carried fire's payer is unnamed for a hundred and ninety-nine days (T088); river, fire and boards keep three counts that do not become one (T061/T082). Sella carries him to the Cross at the half-pace from every open slate, sets the basket in the moot-post's finger's width of shade where no slate lay, stands half a pace off, and gives the instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket; she says the house, keeps her hand off the mark because a reading is not an opening, and gives no reason to the basket (T058/T079). Two hundred lean to the reading block; eight pigs go over the wet boards; the bell goes four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself, the heard kept beside the told (T078). Berr Clay comes up short off the clay road with the red wool cord of his office folded square under his coat and the green of tasted lead glaze at one mouth-corner, wipes his thumb twice before touching nothing, holds a narrow slate unopened to his forearm, passes a finger over the figure, reads One in twelve, as the notice says low into the top of the crowd — the figure going twice over the basket, once for the moot and once for the households that come late — says The levy is called. It is not called by me and your house, never I, and goes off toward High Kiln with the box locked and the true subtraction inside, believing he has done a kindness. This is the chapter's one meaningful change: the district's arithmetic for the kiln month's second reading stands and cannot be undone, while the printed figure stands unchallenged and a figure read aloud is still not the figure paid (T015/T041/T047/T077). Crucially the reading does not answer the man carried out on Day 188: no figure, collector or slate knows what he cost, no collector is called, no cause is named in Grathic and no lesson or account is made of the glaze; his pale line stays on its own place (T064 held). Hessa Rale takes the narrow slate up the road to Greybank before noon edge-on to her forearm, writing turned to her sleeve; to women who ask she says I don't read it. I carry it. There's a difference, and the road doesn't care which and Cross to Greybank. Reading goes up before noon. I've got a road to walk, answering the question put and not the one behind it; her hand goes to the slate before her eyes go to the yard, an eighth record-first hand advanced and not paid, and no figure comes off the slate (T080). A soft-cuffed clerk stays set below the north bridge at the out-of-line landing for a measure nobody called, cuff grey from washing and grey again by midday, hand to slate before eyes to stalls, the market selling over him as water goes over a stone; a measure set down before anybody called it is set down ahead of something, a direction and not a rule (T090). Across the square at the pot board a silent woman with clay under her nails, a pale line across the back of one hand and the sweetish green of lead glaze in the crease beside her lip turns a cup a quarter, sets it back exactly where it stood, says nothing and goes off with the light — the sixth green still a colour joined to no ear, never Fenna in the narration, no seventh green (T050/T051 held). At the market's edge a small shape in cast-off clothes worn like a uniform, silt dried pale in the creases of his wrists, a gap where a front tooth had been and a green sliver of lead glaze on a string at his throat, catches the light and goes dull; his head stops a half-beat toward a pot and he rubs the sliver, unnamed, silent, given no dialogue, no loaf passed, no slate seen, no sale, held as a shape and not counted as a seventh sighting (T033/T034 held). From the basket's low angle the boy reads the order of reaching — Berr's twice-wiped thumb and finger over the figure before his eyes took the crowd, Hessa's hand to the slate before her eyes took the yard, the clerk's hand to the slate before his eyes took the stalls — and keeps each on a place of its own, two records going inward still two records and a row of such hands left standing would call itself an account (T080/T090). Forward, not closed.

scenes.title: What the Reading Did Not Enter
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry of Day 199, no new dated heading: the going of the light and the small hours at the clay road, the Vail roof, the loaf shelf, the kindling, the wheel-shed edge and the bed. Sella carries him home up the clay road at the going of the light with the instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket; woodsmoke goes before her in long low bars and the river wind comes behind with the taste of water over water, the two passing without taking each other's colour; the arm that has carried him a hundred and ninety-nine mornings keeps the height of the handle, the give of the shoulder, the turn of the wrist at a step's end, a record in muscle that remembers weight and not cost. She goes wide around the pan's gone round ring, the bare dark trough whose water is called weather, the rack space with its broken birth-slates, the field's empty place and the place the carriers crossed, each with a look and a wide step and no number; a neighbour's cost-question about what the firing would want now the figure had gone up twice is sent to the pot and the weather and goes away level (T009/T013/T092, T098, T077). Under the roof she sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without a look at his face, leaves the thread frozen, tells the fire it is the thaw and turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, and the fire answers four low pulls with its fifth missing and its payer unnamed for a hundred and ninety-nine days; through the finger's-width door the river keeps its fifth low note and overhead the boards keep four nails, four and a thumb-width knot, three counts in three places that do not become one (T088, T061/T082). At the shelf she moves her lips along the row with two unnamed gaps and gives nobody a figure, glances once at the clay jar without touching it, keeps her finger from beneath the front edge so the charcoal stays unread, and does not touch the widow's mark, for a dusk is not an opening and there has been no opening since before the kiln on Ember 1 (T100, T058/T079). At the kindling Tarn takes the broom only after it is instructed, tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, brings the ear-sentence to the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name, draws the breath he should have spent and does not spend it, says Yes, house to the fire and goes on; nine stoppings stay nine objects with no tenth before the seventh year is earned, the seventh year stands nearer its end than it has ever stood and has not given, the Seed 16 breath is unspent, the loan is uncalled, and his stroke goes over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check (T036/T076). In the wheel-shed Jorra gives the men no name, keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray, tells the wheel and the pot their sayings, withholds the full note known three turns ahead from a wrong wind, and holds his bent finger in the cold damper until Sella's unfinished sentence reaches the pot — a remembered repetition, not a new change, not stood up with 161, 166 or 171; he's not Vail stays sealed and the promise to the slate-burners stays ungiven (T035/T031/T062). In the small hours the boy lays out the file again and finds it exact, complete and worth nothing: six hearings beside and never among with no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and unpaid, the told bell beside the heard, the told figure beside the paid, Berr's box gone up the road locked with the true subtraction inside, Hessa's slate unread at Greybank with no figure coming off it, the soft-cuffed clerk still set for an uncalled measure, three held changes on three places, the loft scrape on a fourth, the pale line on a fifth and the held inch on a sixth, the crust's gap, the shelf's two gaps, the pan's gone ring and the field's empty place on trays that do not touch, no third gap, no fourth likeness, no finger drawn, the stone cold in its loft pot, the charcoal unread, the Seed 16 breath unspent and the loan uncalled (T061/T082, T006, T064, T060/T086/T097, T015/T041/T047, T080/T090). The market's reading has not changed any of it: the district's figure went into the air and not into this house, and a figure read twice is still not the figure paid. Then he puts the question to his own hand and the hand goes up an inch toward the note of water over water and comes down at once with no holding in it — the asking is not always answered — and the miss is filed on the sixth place beside the holdings, not a hearing, not a seventh, not a stopping, not a payment, not a key, not a power and not a rule, no payer named (T061/T082). He still cannot close two inches, lift the crust or speak a number. Forward, not closed.

scenes.title: The Day after the Reading
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry, fifth dated heading: Day 200, Ember 21, Firstday, before first grey through the morning at the Vail roof, the yard well, the drying racks, the wheel-shed edge and up and down the clay road. The month's last tend opens on the morrow, but no boundary is drawn here; the district keeps its two names for the months and neither is corrected. The boy is two hundred days old and six months and twenty days and nobody says so (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth has had no payer for two hundred days (T088); the river, the fire and the boards keep three counts in three places that do not become one (T061/T082). First smell hot clay under tallow and wet wool under that, with the sour mineral breath of the unswept corner; first sound the kiln drawing in fours with a gap, not a bell. Sella's instruction goes to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket; she says the house, keeps her half-pace, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze without a touch, feeds him from the house's own dish with the spoon on her sleeve and not his mouth, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale off the coals, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and lets her hand rest a half-beat longer at the setting (T058/T079). The widow's mark hangs where it hung, for a morning and a shelf are not openings and there has been no opening since before the kiln on Ember 1. At the well a rack woman with slip dried pale in the creases of her wrists asks what the pots will want before the kiln month is out and is told to ask the pot and the weather; a man come off the clay road asks what the kiln will want now the figure has gone up twice and is answered with the house and the weather. Both cost-questions go away level, nothing priced, refused or entered (T077). The sweet edge of lead glaze comes up off High Kiln on a wrong wind and goes out on the same wind, a direction spoken of and answered with the pot and the weather; no second edge is paid so soon after the carrying-out, nobody names the sickness in Grathic, no collector is called and no lesson or account is made of the glaze (T064 held). The yard goes around the clean dark line, the new finer grey called the thaw, the space beneath the lowest rack with its broken birth-slates, the pan's gone round ring with no scrape or chip, the bare dark trough whose water is called weather, the field's empty place in the returning line where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, and the place the carriers crossed, each with a look and a wide step and no number; no third gap comes and no fourth likeness is made a cause (T009/T013/T092, T098, T060/T086/T097). Before first grey three or four men unnamed go low into the finger's-width-open back room and get no name from the house or Jorra; the two shut-room tellings stay two with no third (T065/T095). Jorra comes through with grey slate dust ground small as meal into both forearms past the bent finger, parted from slip as a surgeon parts a clot from its vessel, keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray, asks neither which slate was broken nor whether it was a birth-slate, tells the wheel it does not care whose hands and a pot You'll do, knows the full note three turns ahead and withholds it from a man on a wrong wind whose saying stays a saying about a pot and is not made true as a lesson, no pot lost (T035/T031/T062). When Sella's voice goes low and unfinished his bent finger goes into the cold damper and holds until the sentence reaches the pot, then moves a hair's breadth and is left standing, a remembered repetition and not a change made again (T062). At the kindling Tarn takes the broom only after it is instructed, tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, keeps the knife at the edge of its sill with six counted where the house can check and the seventh at the lip where it cannot, Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it, sweeps the collector's road without turning and no collector comes; the ear-sentence comes to the word that would call the loan and stops with no figure and no name, the Seed 16 breath is unspent, nine stoppings stay nine objects with no tenth before the seventh year is earned, the loan stays uncalled, and his stroke goes over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check (T036/T076). Under the roof in the morning the hand goes up an inch toward the note of water over water, holds for the length of the small intake only and comes down before the letting go — shorter than the longest, the body keeping its own time — filed on its sixth place and not promoted into a hearing, a seventh, a stopping, a payment, a key, a power or a rule, no payer named (T061/T082). The reading is a day behind, gone up the road in a locked box with the printed one in twelve unchallenged and the true subtraction inside; the market does not get to read the inch. Forward, not closed.

scenes.title: The Count Goes Forward
scenes.synopsis: Sixth entry, chapter close, no new dated heading: Day 200, Ember 21, Firstday, afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf, the hearth, the kindling, the wheel-shed edge, the clay road at the going of the light and the bed. The afternoon thins without ending, heat going first off the high air and staying longest under the shelf, behind the pot, in the fold of wool where the boy lies with one leathery crust two inches from his ear and its empty place unnamed, no third; the thread of drool frozen and unwiped; cold stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist joint, afterdrop waiting on a warming nobody will perform. Sella stands with her back to the basket, moves her lips along the row with two unnamed gaps and gives nobody a figure, glances once at the clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing without touching it, keeps her finger from beneath the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, tells the fire it is the thaw and turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it where another woman would say I, stands with the back of the pot counting under her breath toward no opening (the small intake, the hold, the letting go), pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale off the coals, sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, lets her hand rest a half-beat longer at the setting than the setting needs, and does not look toward the bed — she never looks toward the bed at the setting (T058/T079, T100). The widow's mark hangs where it hung, touched once before the kiln on Ember 1 and at no other hour, for a dusk is not an opening. At the kindling the knife lies at the edge of its sill with six counted in the worn thumb-mark and the seventh at the lip, Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it; Tarn takes the broom only after it is instructed, tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, brings the ear-sentence to the threshold of the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name, draws the breath he should have spent and does not spend it, says Yes, house to the fire and goes on; nine stoppings stand as objects with no tenth before the seventh year is earned, the seventh year stands nearer its end than it has ever stood and has not given, the Seed 16 breath is unspent, the loan is uncalled, and his stroke goes over the bright patch without the half-check (T036/T076). In the wheel-shed Jorra gives the men no name, keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray, tells the wheel and the pot their sayings, withholds the note known three turns ahead from a wrong wind, and leaves his bent finger standing in the cold damper after Sella's sentence reaches the pot, a remembered repetition not stood up with the other fractions; the iron is one piece with two bites and no word in Grathic for both mercies, joined to no kiln and entered in no slate; he's not Vail stays sealed and the promise of the boy's name stays ungiven (T035/T031/T062, T065/T095). At the going of the light she carries him home up the clay road with the instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket, woodsmoke before her in long low bars and river wind behind with the taste of water over water, the arm that has carried him two hundred mornings a record in muscle that remembers weight and not cost, going wide around the pan's gone ring, the bare dark trough with its water called weather, the space beneath the lowest rack with its broken birth-slates, the field's empty place and the place the carriers crossed, each with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098). Under the roof she sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without a look at his face, leaves the thread frozen, banks the coals with the back of a broken pot; the fire keeps four low pulls with its fifth missing and no payer for two hundred days, through the finger's-width door the river keeps its fifth low note, overhead the boards keep four nails, four and a knot the width of a thumb — three counts in three places, and none rises up and becomes the others because a man who wanted them to agree would have to put a payer under all three and no payer stands to any (T088, T061/T082). In the small hours he turns out the file as a man lays instruments on a towel: six hearings beside and never among with the sixth from a person and no seventh invented to fill the empty place, three near-full answers advanced and unpaid, the told bell beside the heard, the told figure beside the paid, the box gone up the road locked with the true subtraction inside, Hessa's slate unread at Greybank and the clerk still set for an uncalled measure, three held changes on three places, the loft scrape on a fourth and the carried man's pale line on a fifth, the crust's gap, the shelf's two gaps, the pan's gone ring and the field's empty place on trays that do not touch, no third gap, no fourth likeness made a cause and no finger of his drawing the line, the warm stone cold in its unmarked pot in the loft, the charcoal unread, the Seed 16 breath unspent, the loan uncalled and the cost of the man carried out while the month was young entered nowhere (T061/T082, T006, T064, T060/T086/T097, T100, T015/T041/T047). Then he puts the question to his own hand. The hand outside the wool goes up an inch toward the note of water over water through the finger's-width door, stays up through the whole of one of the breaths Sella counts at her fire in the room that does not touch his — the small intake, the hold and on into the letting go — and comes down with the breath rather than before it, against the fold. It is not a greater reach, not a stronger hand and not a power: it is a coordination with a rhythm in a room he cannot enter, and the rhythm goes on without him and does not stop to notice. He files it on its sixth place of its own beside the others and never lays it across them — not a reaching, not a hearing, not a seventh, not a stopping, not a payment, not one of the three held changes, not a key, not a rule; no payer named and no doctrine stood up out of it. He still cannot close the two inches to the pot handle, lift his chin to the crust or speak a number; the body humiliates him and moves by an inch in the same motion, and both are true. Two hundred stands exact in the dark of the wool, complete and unspent, spoken by nobody under any roof. The carried fire has had no payer for two hundred days; the mark has been touched once before the kiln and at no other hour; the stone is cold in its loft pot; the charcoal under the shelf is unread; the Seed 16 breath is unspent; the loan is uncalled; the cost of the carried man is entered nowhere. The river keeps its fifth low note, the fire misses its fifth pull under the floor and the boards overhead keep four nails, four and a knot the width of a thumb, three counts in three places and none rising up and becoming the others. Nothing has been joined, named, opened, called, spent or ended. The count goes forward into Day 201, Ember 22, Secondday, and the kiln month's last tend begins on an ordinary morning with no boundary drawn.
